scale.zero: First scene (sequence ordinal; not elapsed time)

events.title: Bistritz
events.note: Harker records the journey through Munich, Vienna, Buda-Pesth and Klausenburgh to Bistritz. At the Golden Krone he receives Dracula's letter arranging the onward coach and carriage.

events.title: Crucifix
events.note: The landlady begs Harker to delay his journey because it is the eve of St. George's Day. She gives him a crucifix, and he waits uneasily for the coach.

events.title: Borgo Pass
events.note: Harker recalls the coach journey, the passengers' warnings, and the mysterious driver who meets him at the Borgo Pass. Blue flames and wolves punctuate the night before the carriage reaches the castle.

events.title: Welcome
events.note: Dracula welcomes Harker, carries his luggage and serves him supper without eating. Harker studies his host's unusual appearance and hears wolves outside.

events.title: Carfax
events.note: Harker explores the library and discusses Dracula's wish to master English speech and manners. They review the purchase of Carfax, and their conversation lasts until cockcrow.

events.title: Mirror
events.note: Harker sees no reflection of Dracula in his shaving mirror. The crucifix interrupts the Count's threatening reaction to a cut; Dracula destroys the mirror. Harker then discovers that the castle doors are locked.

events.title: Prisoner
events.note: Harker resolves to conceal his knowledge that he is a prisoner. He observes Dracula performing the work of servants, listens to the Count's account of his ancestry, and notes their conversations ending at cockcrow.

events.title: The wall
events.note: Harker sets out facts about the business arrangements and letters, and records Dracula's warning against sleeping outside his own room. He sees the Count crawl head downward down the castle wall.

events.title: Old rooms
events.note: After seeing Dracula depart down the wall again, Harker explores a disused part of the castle. He finds a room that offers relief from the rooms associated with his host and writes there.

events.title: Three women
events.note: Harker describes falling asleep in the deserted room and encountering three women who approach him with desire and menace. Dracula intervenes, claims him, and offers the women a moving bag from which Harker hears a childlike cry. Harker loses consciousness.
